# `prefer-div-ceil`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Suggests Zig 0.17's `@divCeil` for proven calls to `std.math.divCeil` and for
conservative unsigned ceiling-division patterns such as `(count + block_size -
1) / block_size`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`@divCeil(numerator, denominator)` expresses division rounded toward positive
infinity directly. Adding a rounding adjustment before dividing can overflow
even when the quotient would fit.

## When it fires

This optional idiomatic rule follows immutable aliases of `@import("std")`, its
`math` namespace, and `math.divCeil`. It skips custom helpers, unknown imports,
mutable aliases, and bindings that shadow standard imports. Manual arithmetic
requires a visibly unsigned numerator and a matching positive integer literal,
or immutable aliases of one, as the divisor. Divisors must exceed one. Signed
operands, unknown or mutable divisors, wrapping arithmetic, and different
divisors are excluded.

The standard-library helper remains available in Zig 0.17 and returns an error
union. The builtin requires the caller to guarantee a nonzero divisor and a
representable result. Findings provide advice without an automatic fix, so
existing `try`/`catch` behavior and runtime-safety choices can be reviewed
explicitly. This rule is off by default.

The builtin and its preconditions are described in the [Zig 0.17 release
notes](https://ziglang.org/download/0.17.0/release-notes.html#Added-codedivCeilcode);
the helper's error checks remain in [Zig 0.17's math
implementation](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/src/tag/0.17.0/lib/std/math.zig).

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn blocks(count: u32) !u32 {
    return try std.math.divCeil(u32, count, 8);
}
```
